sections.text: Introduction

This document covers the waste water treatment 
 plant of Talkha PS manufactured by satec Model 18R 100 activated sludge 
 plant, for which secondary and tertiary treatments.

This document initiated by chem. Ahmed-El sayed 
 Metwally reviewed by chem. Adel-Elsayed Hashem by quality control chemist 
 saad sadeek at EDEPC, and approved by Eng: Awad M. Fatthy Head Sector of 
 Talkha Power Station.

This document accepted by eng. Samir Abdel Gilel: EDEPC MPIS coordinator & inspection and
 quality control general director, and certified by 
 accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman EDEPC admin. & financial inspection, 
 quality control general director and supervisor of inspection & quality 
 control Head Sector.
Information
Secondary Treatment

It is a part of Talkha sewage treatment 
 plant in which the sewage flows into the aeration unit and is mixed with a 
 suspension of living aerobic micro-organisms ( activated sludge ) and aerated 
 in a tank by blowing air through the liquid. The micro-organic use the 
 polluting material in the sewage as food and convert it to carbon dioxide, 
 water and new cell material to 
 maintain efficient mixing and provide the oxygen which the organisms need. The 
 micro-organisms use the polluting matter in the sewage as food and convert it 
 to carbon dioxide, water and new cell material. The aeration of the mixed 
 liquor ( mixture of sewage and activated sludge ) provides the organisms with 
 oxygen and also helps to mix the contents of the tank.
PH

Bacteria + Organic Matter + O2 ----------> CO2 
 + H2O + New Cell

After several hours aeration, the mixture liquor passes into the 
 settlement tank where the activated sludge settles and is returned to the 
 aeration tank for reuse ( via a return sludge airlift ) to treat more sewage. The clear 
 liquid supernatant at the surface of the settlement tank contains very little 
 residual organic material and can generally be discharged direct to a 
 water course as treated effluent or as in this case given further treatment to 
 improve the quality by, (via Dual Media Filtration ) which removes the fine 
 suspended solidest, and sterilized ( via hypochlorite ).

Excess activated sludge (cell material ) has to 
 be periodically removed to optimize the plant efficiency. A surplus activated 
 sludge airlift transfers sludge from the aeration tank ( via the settlement 
 tank ) into an aerobic sludge digester, which is aerated by blowing air 
 through the liquor. The sludge (with oxygen but without external food) digests 
 itself to produce a carbon dioxide, water and a much reduced volume of sludge.

In the satec plant, the aeration, settlement and 
 aerobic sludge digestion phases occur continuously.

In addition, as excess sludge builds up in the 
 plant and digester, it is necessary to remove or waste some sludge 
 from the plant to maintain the correct balance. In this plant this achieved 
 manually by draining off some wastes sludge from the digester to the drying 
 beds to produce a low volume cake.

The activated sludge is a very complex mixture of 
 micro-organisms which can rapidly fluctuate and show very marked variations at 
 different locations.

Bacteria
 The most important group of micro-organisms in 
 the aerobic biological treatment of sewage/effluent. These are small, less 
 than 1m in diameter and less than 5 
 m in length, and occur in many forms in 
 countless numbers. Bacteria utilise substances in true solution and have very 
 fast growth rates and operate most efficiently at pH between (6.5 and 8.5 ).

Fungi
 Multi-cellular plant-like organisms which use organic matter as their food 
 supply. These can operate at much lower pH 
 values than bacteria but, since they tend to be difficult to settle because 
 of their filamentous nature, operating conditions are arranged to discourage 
 their formation.

sections.text: Plant Description

items:
Screening or Comminuter Unit 
 Sewage or trade waste flows into the plant through either a screen or 
 comminutor. The function of comminutor is to chop up solids such as rags 
 without removing them from the sewage flow.

Aeration Compartments 
 The annular aeration compartments containing the mixed liquor are fitted with 
 coarse bubble air diffusers supported in clusters on down-pipes connected to 
 the air header. Each individual down-pipe is equipped with a stop-cock, for 
 regulating their supply and allowing the downpipe with its diffuser cluster 
 to be removed from the aeration tank whilst the plant is in operation.

sections.text: Operating Directives

The main points 
requiring attention to ensure correct operation of the plant are dissolved 
oxygen concentration, mixed liquor suspended solid concentration, mixed liquor 
pH, and sludge quality.

Dissolved Oxygen Concentration-
The concentration of dissolved oxygen not below 0.5 mg/l.

Mixed Liquor Suspended Solid Concentration-
The concentration of suspended solid in the mixed liquor in the mixing aeration 
tank should be maintained in the region of 2000-3000 mg/l with a rapidly 
settling activated sludge, this will correspond to a volume of approximately 25-40 % after settlement for 30 minutes.

Mixed Liquor pH-
For the correct functioning of the biological process the mixed liquor should be 
in the range pH 6.5 8.0.

Foam Control-
This may be controlled by the addition of small quantity
90.1 liters-1/4 pt )of thefoam oil.

F/M Ratio = Influent B.O.D in 
(kg/day) / MLVSS (kg) x 
aeration tank volume.
MLVSS mean (mixed liquor volatile suspended solids ). This ratio may be 
equal 0.15 for a good operation which we can adjust the amount of activated 
return sludge from the settling tank to the aeration tank.

sections.text:
Operating 
Tests

Settlement Test
This simple test 
provides basic information regarding the operation of the plant and should be 
carried out daily.
A one liter 
measuring cylinder should be filled with mixed liquor from the mixing aeration 
compartment and allowed to stand for 30 minutes.
The volume of sludge settled 
out should normally be in the range 25-40 %. If the volume is above 40 % the 
mixed liquor should be checked. 
The supernatant liquor above the sludge layer should be clear, free from 
excessive solids layer and should have a faint earthy smell. 
A smell of H2S indicates that the 
air supply to the plant is an inadequate and should be increased. 
The sludge 
should be dark brown in colour, a grey or black colour also indicates inadequate air supply.

Dissolved Oxygen
A good 
indication that the dissolved oxygen concentration is sufficient is given by 
superficial is examination of the mixed liquor. The mixed liquor should have 
only a faint earthy smell. A black or grey mixed liquor having a foul smell 
indicates that the air supply is insufficient and this should be increased, we 
can measure the oxygen by a dissolved oxygen meter, and can be measured 
chemically using the (copper sulphate-sulphamic acid 
method ).

pH
The 
determination of mixed liquor pH is best carried out by the use of an electronic 
pH meter or by the use of pH indicator papers of the appropriate range.

sections.text:
Maintenance 
of Mechanical Equipment

Aeration Tank
The walls of the aeration tanks above the water line should be kept clean and 
free from grease and scum by brushing and/ or hosing as the required air diffuser 
should be inspected every two months and cleaned.

Air Lifts
The sludge 
return air lift should be in operation all the time and only requires attention 
in the event of a blockage.
If should the air lift become blocked it must be freed 
immediately.

Air Blower 
It should be 
lubricated and cleaned weekly by brushing and 
washing-changing 
the blower drive motor belts.
The blowers 
have been provided with spare drive belts and when 
necessary these are changed in the following manner:
 * Turn 
the power off by closing the locally sited isolator and also the associated 
isolator on the control plant, for added safety remove the appropriate fuses.
 * Open 
the belt guard.
 * Remove the existing V belts, it may be necessary to slacken off the belts 
first by moving the motor along the side rails.
 * Replace the belts with those provided and re-tighten the motor 
side 
rails ensuring that the belts are tensioned correctly and the pulleys are 
correctly aligned.
 * Replace the belts guard and restart the blower.

Electric 
Motors 
It must be cleaned, maximum permissible temperature rise of the motor is 65C. Lubrication should 
be carried out in accordance with the manufacture's instructions.
